text: In your science class, which experiment would you find most exciting to do?

options.text: Building an electric circuit and testing how voltage affects a bulb
Looking at cells under a microscope and drawing what I see
Mixing chemicals to see which combinations cause a reaction
Conducting a survey about students' study habits and making charts

text: If your school gave you a free afternoon to work on any project, which would you pick?

options.text: Programming a small game or app on a computer
Designing a model of a building or bridge using cardboard and sticks
Running a small shop in school — buying, selling, tracking profit and loss
Writing and performing a short play or creating a school newspaper

text: Which of these school subjects do you look forward to the most?

options.text: Mathematics — especially when solving equations and geometry problems
Biology — understanding how the human body and living things work
Social Science or Economics — understanding money, trade, and how societies work
Language or History — reading stories, debating, and writing essays

text: Your colony has a problem: the water supply cuts out every afternoon. How would you approach solving it?

options.text: Design a rainwater collection and storage system with pipes and tanks
Test the water quality and check if the source is contaminated
Gather the residents, write a formal petition to the municipality
Calculate how much water is needed per day and propose a budget to dig a borewell

text: How do you prefer to understand something new?

options.text: By working through formulas, diagrams, and solving step-by-step problems
By observing real specimens or watching biological or chemical processes happen
By reading about it, discussing it with others, and forming opinions
By physically building it, taking it apart, and seeing how it works with my hands

text: Which of these people's jobs would you most like to have when you grow up?

options.text: A doctor who diagnoses diseases and helps patients recover
A software engineer who builds apps used by millions of people
A Chartered Accountant who manages finances for large companies
A lawyer who argues cases in court and fights for justice

text: Imagine your future job. Which kind of workplace would make you happiest?

options.text: An office or studio where I work with computers and technology every day
An outdoor construction site or engineering project — seeing real things built
A hospital or clinic — helping people with their health every day
A courtroom, newsroom, or school — working with people, ideas, and words

text: When you solve a difficult maths problem and get the right answer, how do you feel?

options.text: Very satisfied — I enjoy the logical process of working through maths
Okay — maths is fine when it's about measuring or calculating real things
Relieved — I find maths hard but I can manage it when needed
Not for me — I strongly prefer reading, writing, and discussing ideas

text: You're standing in front of a bridge. What goes through your mind first?

options.text: How do the steel cables and beams hold all that weight safely?
The design is beautiful — how did they make it look so elegant?
Is the construction affecting the river ecosystem below?
What did this cost, who funded it, and how is it maintained?

text: Which of these best describes how you like to spend your free time?

options.text: Watching tutorial videos and trying to build websites or small programs
Sketching, painting, or creating digital art and designs
Gardening, tending to plants, or learning about farming techniques
Reading books, writing stories or poetry, keeping a journal

text: If a classmate is struggling with a personal problem, what do you naturally do?

options.text: Listen carefully, ask questions, and try to understand exactly how they feel
Help them find a practical solution — give them advice and action steps
Suggest they talk to the school counselor or a trusted adult
I'm not the best at this — I prefer working with ideas and systems more than people problems

text: When you use a phone or computer, which activity interests you the most?

options.text: Building or customizing an app or website — the creation process itself
Analyzing data — looking at YouTube analytics, player statistics, or trends
Making the interface look better — colors, fonts, buttons, and layout
Creating content — videos, blogs, social media posts, or podcasts

text: After 10th, which educational path feels most appealing to you right now?

options.text: Science stream in Class 11–12, then a college degree
Commerce stream in Class 11–12, then a finance or business degree
Arts/Humanities stream in Class 11–12, then law, journalism, or social sciences
A 3-year polytechnic diploma — get into a job sooner

text: Which type of difference would you most like to make in the world someday?

options.text: Saving lives — curing diseases and improving healthcare for poor communities
Protecting the environment — fighting climate change and saving ecosystems
Building the nation — good governance and making government work for people
Creating jobs — building a successful business that employs thousands

text: Your teacher asks why plants near a road grow slower than those in a garden. What's your approach to finding out?

options.text: Study the plants' biology — check their leaves, roots, and internal processes
Test the soil and air near the road for pollutants and chemicals
Collect data on sunlight, water, and temperature differences between the two locations
Research what scientists have already published about road pollution and plant growth

text: When it comes to your future career, which statement fits you best?

options.text: I'd rather build my own business, even if it means uncertainty and risk
I want a stable government job — security and service matter more than high salary
I want a well-paying private sector career — good salary with some stability
I want to do something deeply meaningful, even if it takes many years of study

text: Which type of reading do you enjoy the most?

options.text: Novels, poetry, or plays that explore human emotions and stories
News articles about business, the economy, or stock markets
Science books or magazines about discoveries, space, or technology
Books about history, politics, biographies of leaders, or social issues

text: Given a real problem that needs solving, which approach excites you most?

options.text: Draw and design a creative solution — buildings, products, or visual layouts
Write code — automate it, build a tool, or design a digital system
Research it deeply — find the cause, look at precedent, write a report with recommendations
Investigate it scientifically — run experiments and test possible medical or biological causes

text: How do you prefer to learn about a complex machine (like a car engine)?

options.text: I want to study the deep physics and mathematical formulas that explain how the engine works.
I want to take a 3-year hands-on course immediately to learn how to design and fix these machines in a factory.
I want to start an apprenticeship or quick training to become an expert mechanic as soon as possible.
I am not interested in machines; I prefer studying living things or business.

text: When thinking about biology and mathematics, which statement best describes you?

options.text: I only want to study biology to become a doctor. I do not want to study mathematics anymore.
I love biology, but I also want to keep mathematics as a backup in case I want to pursue biotechnology or engineering.
I only want to study mathematics and physics. Biology is not for me.
I am not highly interested in either; I prefer social sciences or accounts.

text: If you were to read a non-fiction book, which topic would you choose?

options.text: How successful companies manage their money, invest, and grow the economy.
The history of ancient civilizations, human psychology, and political movements.
New discoveries in space exploration, medical research, and technology.
A guide on how to build, repair, and troubleshoot everyday electronics.

text: If you decided not to study 11th and 12th standard, what would you rather do?

options.text: Join a 3-year Polytechnic Diploma to become a Junior Engineer.
Join a 1 or 2-year ITI course to quickly master a specific skill like plumbing or drafting.
I definitely want to study 11th and 12th standard in a Science stream.
I definitely want to study 11th and 12th standard in Commerce or Arts.
